scope: Completed 500-year fixed-pressure reference, panels S5a and S5b, and the S5 composite with previously audited coupled panels; verification is limited to this case and figure.
checks: Full accepted history and all saved fields pass the separately recorded raw-output audit, including constant effective stress in the fixed-pressure run.
Panel time, accepted step, depth, initial profile and field arrays exactly match the selected independent binary output.
Cumulative slip is zeroed at the first selected snapshot; every plotted profile and its class match the documented four-year and one-second selection rules.
Cycle bounds and recurrence comparisons agree with complete large-event end times; S5b contains the last two complete cycles.
All plotted numerical arrays are finite; data/figure files are below 100 MiB; source, configuration and plotting provenance agree with the current files.

visual_review.reference: Published Supplementary Figure 5, PDF page 6, inspected only as a visual comparison target.
findings: Both time and accepted-step velocity maps, two cumulative-slip cycles, units and the combined four-panel figure are legible.

The final calculated reference interval is 95.06 years, compared with approximately 160 years in the published example. All three calculated intervals are retained and no stationary-period claim is made.

The calculated deep partial rupture spans 10.12--17.89 km by the connected 1 cm criterion and peaks only 2.37 hours before the closing large event. The published map places its partial rupture much earlier in the cycle.

The closing large event first exceeds the speed threshold near 0.525 km depth and propagates downward in the generated step map. This differs from the deep-to-shallow closing rupture visible in the published reference.
Two calculated cycles accumulate 5.57 m of shallow slip; the published two-cycle profile extends to about 12 m. This is a visual comparison scale, not a digitized curve or model input.

The time map ends at the closing earthquake; its short seismic intervals are compressed at the right edge, whereas the published map includes a post-earthquake tail. The accepted-step view resolves the rupture ordering but its step count is not a physical accuracy metric.

Saved-profile cadence produces steps in the accepted-step map. The minimum nucleation length spans 4.29 cells, and this high-healing-time reference has no separate spatial refinement study. Both new panels remain partial.
